questions.question: Describe about: a) Thermophillic bacterias b) Psychrotropic bacterias c) Halotolerant bacterias d) Aciduric bacterias
questions.solution_html:
• Describe about a) Thermophilicbacterias b) Psychrotropicbacterias c)
  • Halotolerantbacterias d) Aciduric bacterias
  • a) Thermophilic Bacteria
  • • Thrive at high temperatures (45–70°C).
  • • Commonly found in hot springs, compost, and industrial heaters.
  • • In food, they spoil canned foods, dehydrated foods, milk powders.
  • • Examples: Bacillus stearothermophilus, Thermus spp.
  • • Their spores survive heat → important in thermal processing.
  • b) Psychrotropic Bacteria
  • • Grow at low temperatures (0–7°C) but optimum at 20–30°C.
  • • Responsible for spoilage of refrigerated foods.
  • • Produce lipases and proteases that survive pasteurization.
  • • Examples: Pseudomonas, Listeria monocytogenes.
  • • Cause spoilage in milk, meat, fish, vegetables.
  • c) Halotolerant Bacteria
  • • Can grow in high salt concentrations, but do not require salt.
  • • Found in salted foods, cured meats, pickles, fish sauces.
  • • Example: Staphylococcus aureus (food poisoning bacteria).
  • • Important in food preservation, fermented foods.
  • • Spoilage risk in salted products if hygiene is poor.
  • d) Aciduric Bacteria
  • • Survive and grow in low pH (acidic) foods.
  • • Common in fruits, juices, pickles, fermented foods.
  • • Examples: Lactobacillus, Acetobacter, Leuconostoc.
  • • Responsible for spoilage of acidic beverages.
  • • Important in food fermentation (e.g., yogurt, sauerkraut).
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
questions.final_answer: • Important in food fermentation (e.g., yogurt, sauerkraut).

questions.question: Explain how food regulates various bodily activities
questions.solution_html:
• Explain how food regulates various bodily activities
  • • Provides energy for all body processes.
  • • Proteins help growth, repair, and build enzymes and hormones.
  • • Vitamins and minerals regulate metabolic reactions.
  • • Fats support hormone production and temperature regulation.
  • • Minerals maintain fluid balance, nerve impulses, and muscle function.
  • • Nutrients support strong immunity.
  • • Dietary fiber regulates digestion and bowel movement.
  • • B-vitamins support brain and nervous system function.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
questions.final_answer: • B-vitamins support brain and nervous system function.

questions.question: Describe the role of world health organization in promoting global food safety.
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the role of world health organization in promoting global food safety
  • • Develops international food standards (Codex Alimentarius).
  • • Conducts global surveillance of foodborne diseases.
  • • Provides scientific risk assessments on contaminants and additives.
  • • Helps countries strengthen food safety laws and systems.
  • • Issues guidelines on hygiene and safe food handling.
  • • Promotes awareness through programs
  • • Coordinates international response to food safety emergencies.
  • • Supports training, research, and capacity building.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
questions.final_answer: • Supports training, research, and capacity building.

questions.question: Write a note on minerals
questions.solution_html:
• Write a note on minerals
  • • Needed in small amounts but vital for health.
  • • Types of Minerals:
  • • Macrominerals: Calcium, phosphorus, magnesium, sodium, potassium, chloride.
  • • Trace minerals: Iron, zinc, iodine, copper, selenium, fluoride.
  • • Functions:
  • • Bone formation: Calcium, phosphorus.
  • • Muscle contraction and nerve transmission: Sodium, potassium.
  • • Oxygen transport: Iron.
  • • Thyroid hormone formation: Iodine.
  • • Antioxidant defense: Selenium.
  • • Sources:
  • • Milk, leafy vegetables, nuts, meat, cereals, and fruits.
  • • Deficiency Effects:
  • • Iron deficiency: Anemia
  • • Iodine deficiency: Goiter
  • • Calcium deficiency: Osteoporosis
  • • Toxicity:
  • • Excess intake may cause health issues, e.g., high sodium → hypertension.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
questions.final_answer: • Excess intake may cause health issues, e.g., high sodium → hypertension.

questions.question: Mention the importance of protein in food
questions.solution_html:
• Mention the importance of protein in food
  • • Proteins help in growth and repair of body tissues.
  • • They form enzymes that control digestion and metabolic activities.
  • • They help in the production of hormones such as insulin.
  • • Proteins build antibodies and support the immune system.
  • • They help maintain fluid and electrolyte balance in the body.
  • • Proteins act as an energy source when carbohydrates and fats are insufficient.
  • • They transport and store important substances (example: hemoglobin transports
  • oxygen).
  • • Proteins provide structure to muscles, skin, hair, and nails.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
questions.final_answer: • Proteins provide structure to muscles, skin, hair, and nails.

questions.question: Evaluate and conclude the most controllable hazard in food with reasons Type Questions
questions.solution_html:
• Evaluate and conclude the most controllable hazard in food with reasons
  • Food hazards are biological, chemical, and physical.Among these, physical hazards
  • are the most controllable.
  • Reasons:
  • • Physical hazards like glass, metal, stones, and plastic pieces are easy to detect.
  • • They can be prevented through simple measures like proper cleaning, inspection,
  • and equipment maintenance.
  • • Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) such as sieving, filtering, and visual
  • checking help control these hazards.
  • • Physical hazards do not multiply or grow over time, unlike biological hazards.
  • • Their prevention does not depend on temperature, pH, or moisture conditions.
  • Physical hazards are the most controllable because they are visible, easily preventable, and
  • can be eliminated through basic quality-control practices.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
questions.final_answer: can be eliminated through basic quality-control practices.

questions.question: Write a note on fats
questions.solution_html:
• Write a note on fats
  • • Fats are essential macronutrients that provide concentrated energy to the body.
  • • They supply 9 kcal of energy per gram, which is higher than carbohydrates and
  • proteins.
  • • Fats help in the absorption of fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E, and K.
  • • They provide essential fatty acids such as omega-3 and omega-6, which the body
  • cannot synthesize.
  • • Fats maintain body temperature by acting as an insulator.
  • • They form cell membranes and support normal cell function.
  • • Fats enhance the flavour, texture, and palatability of food.
  • • They serve as a protective cushion for internal organs.
  • • Moderate intake of healthy fats supports brain and hormone function.
  • • Excessive intake of saturated and trans fats leads to obesity, heart disease, and
  • metabolic disorders.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
questions.final_answer: metabolic disorders.

questions.question: Explain Quality Assurance in food industry.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain Quality Assurance in food industry
  • • Quality Assurance (QA) is a systematic approach to ensure food products meet
  • safety and quality standards.
  • • QA focuses on preventing defects rather than detecting them after production.
  • • It involves the implementation of Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP).
  • • Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) are developed and followed to maintain
  • consistency.
  • • QA ensures compliance with national and international food regulations.
  • • Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point (HACCP) is used to identify and
  • control hazards.
  • • Regular inspections, audits, and documentation help maintain quality.
  • • QA includes training workers to maintain hygiene and follow safety protocols.
  • • It ensures traceability by keeping proper records from raw materials to finished
  • products.
  • • QA builds consumer trust, reduces product recalls, and improves overall
  • productivity.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
questions.final_answer: productivity.

questions.question: Explain about the causes of Food insecurity.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain about the causes of Food insecurity
  • • Poverty is the major cause of food insecurity because people cannot afford
  • nutritious food.
  • • Climate change leads to droughts, floods, and reduced crop production.
  • • Rapid population growth increases demand for food resources.
  • • Poor agricultural productivity affects the availability of food.
  • • Political instability disrupts food supply chains and access.
  • • Unemployment reduces purchasing power, increasing food insecurity.
  • • Natural disasters destroy crops, livestock, and infrastructure.
  • • Lack of access to land and water resources affects farmers' ability to grow food.
  • • Inefficient storage and transportation systems lead to post-harvest losses.
  • • Rising food prices make essential staples difficult for low-income families to buy.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
questions.final_answer: • Rising food prices make essential staples difficult for low-income families to buy.
